title: Confidence in action
html:
Yesterday I saw Craig Lowndes racing up Bathurst's Mountain Straight with one hand on the steering wheel, changing gears when he needed to, and looking very relaxed at 250km/hr.

If you have never been that fast you might wonder how he can do that, or how motorcycle racers can look behind them, or use their tear-offs at similar speeds and even in mid corner.

It comes down to confidence. Confidence in your ability, confidence in your machine, confidence in the other racers’ ability, confidence in knowing where you are on the track and, for some reason, at times like this, time seems to actually slow down for you.

How does this apply to you? You do things everyday without thinking, and even though it might not seem so, time slows down for you too. You have confidence to do those things without thinking.

Now you might not see this confidence straight away, but I know that there are things you can do that seem effortless to you. Your knowledge and experience will combine to create the same confidence Craig Lowndes has at 250km/hr.

Take a look at what comes to you effortlessly and you will see confidence in action. Confidence you can use to help you through those things that you can't do so well yet.
